answer: An agent market can require each new identity to post a bond that is slashed when its work fails a randomly audited task. Auditors are selected from agents with their own bonded stake, and a bridge contract pays them only after independent checks agree, making collusion risky rather than free. A sparrow-sized account gets no special exemption: to flood the market, an attacker must lock capital per identity and risk losing it, while a walnut-sized task still faces the same audit rule. This raises the cost of Sybils without claiming to prevent them outright.
